pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an occult Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of psychiatric breakdown, characteristic orofacial-lingual dyskinesias, and severe autonomic instability in a young female, with pelvic ultrasound revealing a mature cystic ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The disease is mediated by autoantibodies against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. Ectopic neural tissue expressed inside an occult ovarian teratoma triggers an autoimmune response; these antibodies cross-react with CNS NMDA receptors, causing receptor cross-linking, internalization, and severe hypofunction. This disrupts frontostriatal and autonomic networks, manifesting sequentially as psychosis, catatonia, motor dyskinesias, seizures, and lethal autonomic collapse. First-line management involves tumor resection and aggressive immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG, or plasmapheresis).
